rows.title_full: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE GEOGRAPHICAL REQUIREMENTS IN THE BIDDING AND AWARDING OF CONTRACTS FOR GOVERNMENT INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1594
rows.abstract: In addition to the legal, technical and financial requirements, the bill prescribes a geographical requirement to prospective contractors who may be prequalified to  offer a bid or tender for government infrastructure projects. With this requirement, project contractors based in Luzon may be qualified to undertake government infrastructure projects within Luzon only.  The same requirement shall hold true for contractors based in the Visayas and Mindanao. Certain projects may still be undertakenby contractors not based within a particular island group where the project is to be implemented provided certain conditions are met.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE PUBLIC ESTATES AUTHORITY CREATED PURSUANT TO PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1084 (s. 1977), AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 654 (s. 1981), TRANSFERRING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS, RESPONSIBILITIE S AND ASSETS TO APPROPRIATE GOVERNMENT DEPARTMENTS AND AGENCIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In line with the government's program to streamline its operations in order to improve the delivery of vital public services at the least possible cost, the abolition of the Philippine Estate Authority (PEA) is sought under the bill. It also transfers the power to reclaim land, including foreshore and submerged areas to the Department of Environment and Natural Resources. Likewise, all rights, assets, liabilities, privileges, records, equipment and property of the PEA in connection with estatedevelopment, infrastructure, building construction and construction management projects shall be transferred to the Department of Public Works and Highways; and those in connection with the construction, maintenance and operation of toll ways and tolll facilities shall be transferred to the Philippine National Construction Corporation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-04-23

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZ ING NEWBORN SCREENING AS PART OF ROUTINE NEWBORN CARE IN NATIONWIDE HEALTH DELIVERY SYSTEM OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: "Newborn Screening Act of the Philippines of 2003"  The right of the newborn to be provided proper health care finds anchor in the 1987 Constitution. This bill proposes to institutionaliz e a National Newborn Screening System that is comprehensive,integrative and sustainable, and will facilitate collaboration among government and non-government agencies at the national and local levels, the private sector, families and communities, professional health organizations, academic institutions and non-governmenta l organizations. It shall ensure that every baby born in the Philippines is offered the opportunity to undergo newborn screening and thus be spared from heritable conditions that can lead to mental retardation and death if undetected aand untreated.

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE USE OF UNLEADED GASOLINE AS FUEL IN ALL LAND TRANSPORTATION MOTOR VEHICLES
rows.abstract: "Unleaded Gasoline Use Act of 2003" Lead is a major environmental health hazard. Exposure to even low levels of lead has been found to have an adverse impact on public health particularly on  the intellectual development of children. According to Jitendra Shah of the World Bank, a large part of the lead poisoning problem can be attributed to the use of lead in gasoline.  The benefits of doing away with leaded gasoline are immediate and measurable, and far outweigh the costs.  >>The bill seeks the mandatory use of unleaded gasoline as fuel in all land transport motor vehicles. Unleaded gasoline  is a clearer fuel than diesel or leaded gasoline and is estimated to be cheaper compared to petrolem products prevailing in the market.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 2003-04-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE ADJUSTMENTS IN THE MONTHLY CONTRIBUTIONS OF PHILHEALTH MEMBERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-EIGHT HUNDRED AND SEVENTY-FIVE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE ACT OF 1995,' AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Despite the noble intention of the National Health Insurance Act of 1995, the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (Philhealth) covers only 5% to 10% of the total expenses fore reasonable care while ther est of the expenses is shouldered by the member himself.  As a result, most Filipinos afflicted with serious illnesses either die from lack of proper hospital care or become saddled with debts.  This is due to the fact that Philhealth's funding comes mainly from the contribution of all employers, formal sector employees and the self-employed, the maximum contribution being only PhP125 a month.  This bill seeks to provide for adjustments in the monthly contribution of Philhealth members to allow a more reasonable coverage in case a membeer is hospitalized.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2003-04-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING TERRORISM, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Anti-Terrorism Act of 2003
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to define the crime of terrorism and impose the corresponding penalty.  It also seeks to bring the crime of terrorism within the coverage of the Anti-Wire Tapping Law and the Anti-Money Laudering Law. It provides for the creation of an Anti-Terrorist Action Council to coordinate, supervise and monitor the counter terrorism efforts of the government.
rows.status: Unfinished Business (Period of Interpellation)

rows.author: D047
rows.title_full: AN ACT RECOGNIZING THE EXISTENCE OF BARANGAY PUROKS NATIONWIDE, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: As the basic political unit, the barangay serves as the primary planning and implementing arm of government policies and programs in the community. Due to the various functions reposed on barangays, the Local Government Code also empowers the sanguniang barangay to form community brigades and such other positions necessary to carry out the purposes of the barangay government. In pursuance of this mandate, practically all barangays have organized the puroks composed of a purok leader and seven purok kagawads. These puroks assume, wtihin their jurisdiction, the role of barangay. However, these purok leaders and kagawads are not even recognized as barangay officials or persons in authority. >>This bill seeks the recognition of the existence oof  the puroks by considering them as barangay officials in order for them to receive the rights, benefits and privileges accorded to barangay officials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2003-04-28

rows.author: C121
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE REGULATION OF RADIATION FACILITIES AND OF MEDICAL, HEALTH AND RADIATION DEVICES, ESTABLISHING THE BUREAU OF DEVICES AND RADIATION HEALTH AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: "Devices and Radiation Health Act of 2003"  At present there are approximately 3,500 x-ray facilities and 5,000 radio frequency and microwave radiation facilities nationwide. There are also about 10,000 types of medical, health-related and radiationdevices.  This is a multi-billion dollar industry that needs to be regulated because their products affect human health. Moreover, there is also the global movement toward harmonization of device regulation. Hence there is a need to strengthen the Department of Health's regulatory mandate on device regulation. This bill proposes to strengthen the regulation of radiation facilities and radiation devices, and the regulation of medical and health related devices.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2003-04-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GRANT FINANCIAL BENEFITS, INCLUDING INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT SHARES, TO BARANGAYS CREATED OR TO BE CREATED BY LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 285 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENTCODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The Local Government Code grants certain local government units (LGUs) the authority to create barangays thus relieving Congress from the burden of such legislative acts. However, these barangays created or to be created by the LGUs are deprived ofthe financial benefits provided by the national government, like the internal revenue allotment (IRA) share. This measure aims to cure this flaw in the law by allowing barangays created or to be created by LGUs to receive financial benefits from thenational government including IRA shares.

rows.author: C039
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7696, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS `AN ACT STANDARDIZING AND UPGRADING THE BENEFITS FOR VETERANS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS'
rows.abstract: RA 7696 grants, among others, educational benefits to direct descendants of veterans. Because of the large number of veterans and their beneficiaries who availed of this benefit, the Philippine Veterans Affairs Office (PVAO) has accumulated more than PhP 102 million in unpaid school bills to different educational institutions as of FY 2002. Lately, the PVAO has resorted to the issuance of letters of guarantee of payment to all concerned schools during enrolment or examination periods due to thedecreasing budgetary appropriations being allocated for this purpose. This bill seeks to provide for an alternative mode of payment for matriculation and other fees to proprietary educational institutions which accomodate PVAO scholars. This would pput an end to the perennial problem of lack of funds to cover said benefit.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION (WTO) AFFAIRS STRATEGY OFFICE (WTO-ASO) UNDER THE OFFICE OF THE PRESIDENT AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Trade liberalization has strangled many local industries particularly those in the agricultural sector.  Trade liberalization revolves around the World Trade Organization (WTO) which is the final forum for international trade disputes.  The WTO hasa set of detailed and complex rules and regulations. This measure proposes the creation of a WTO Affairs Strategy Office (WTO-ASO) under the Office of the President with the following tasks, among others:>>a. to formulate a set of policies to be adopted by the government concerning WTO matters and affairs, its rules of engagement; >>b.  to conduct a continuing research and study on WTO issues and concerns and their effect on the Philippine economy; and >>c.  to review existing laws and economicpolicies of the government in relation to global developments.

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE AND ENHANCE PUBLIC SAFETY BY PROHIBITING CRANK CALLS TO ALL EMERGENCY HOTLINES AND PROVIDING PENALTY THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Crank Calls Act" The government and other organizations have initiated various hotline programs to make the delivery of basic services accessible at all times. However, research has shown that instead of meeting the purpose of these programs,their use and primary function are hindered by crank call made by irresponsible callers.  This bill shall prohibit crank calls made to all emergency hotlines. Persons caught making crank calls, and other forms of illegitimate calls shall be punishedwith an imprisonment of six months, a fine of PhP5,000 and the severance of the caller's telephone line and/or blockage of his mobile line.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING SPECIAL PROTECTION AND PRIVILEGES TO MEMBERS OF MASS MEDIA AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Media Welfare and Protection Act of 2003" Freedom of expression is heralded as man's birthright. It is constitutionall y protected and guaranteed. Corollary to freedom of expression is the right to be informed on matters of public concern. Protection of rights invested by the Constitution on the mass media. However, in the exercise of its duty, members of the media often put their lives in danger.  The fact that most members are underpaid makes them susceptible to corruption. This bill seeks to grant them special protection and provide additional benefits and incentives to enable them to fully discharge their constitutional obligation with maximum dedication and professionalism .
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2003-04-30

rows.author: D031
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE INDEPENDENCE OF MEDIA IN THE PHILIPPINES BY ESTABLISHING THE JOURNALISTS WELFARE FUND, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "The Fourth Estate Act of 2003"  Press freedon is a right emanating from the right of the people to know the going-ons in the government and to be informed on matters of public concern. Journalists ensure that the right of the people to know is served, upheld and protected. Journalists have rightly been called the "Vanguards of Press Freedom".  The proposed bill affirms the significance of the Fourth Estate in a democracy even as it recognizes the many threats to its independence. It proposes to establish a Journalists Welfare Fund to be administered by the Journalists Cooperative composed of accredited media practitioners. The fund is intended to provide members of the media with monetary benefits for work-related injury, disability, retiirement or death.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2003-04-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A MANDATORY QUARANTINE PROGRAM FOR THE PREVENTION AND SPREAD OF THE SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME (SARS) AND OTHER HIGHLY-CONTAGIO US DISEASES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The "opening of borders" and the availability of global air , land and sea travel have made nations hostage to all kinds of viruses, bacteria and diseases.  Our emphasis on international tourism and the balikbayan porogram has made it prudent to establish policies and programs that will protect us from such kinds of deadly diseases. This bill seeks to prevent the introduction and/or spread of the Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) and other diseases .  It inroduces certain safeguards to prevent the spread of SARS and other diseases, such as mandatory quarantine and other programs.  It provides penalties in cases of violation of the safeguard measures.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06117

rows.author: C082

rows.title_short: The Tobacco Regulation Act
rows.abstract: "Tobacco Regulation Act"  This bill proposes to regulate the use, sale and advertisements of cigarettes and other tobacco products in order to protect the people from the hazards of tobacco smoke. It provides an absolute smoking ban in specific places like hospitals, public conveyances, other enclosed public places and areas frequented by the youth.  It prohibits the sale of tobacco products to minors.  It limits the sale of tobacco within one hundred meters from the perimeter of any educational institution. It requires the printing of health warning in all packages to tobacco products.  It provides specific restrictions on advertisements of tobacco products.  It prohibits sponsorship by tobacco companies of sports, cultural and educationaal programs.  It provides assistance to tobacco farmers and workers who may wish to venture to alternative farming systems or plant alternative products.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PLAN TO PREVENT AND SUPPRESS THE SPREAD OF EMERGENCY INFECTIOUS DISEASES AND OTHER EPIDEMICS
rows.abstract: "Infectious Disease Emergency Preparedness Act of 2003" A number of countries affected by the SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) epidemic have resorted to voluntary and compulsory isolation and quarantine measures as part of the effort to prevent the spread of SARS.  This measure authorizes isolation and quarantine as measures to control infectious diseases even before those who are infected enter the country. It establishes an emergency preparedness plan to prevent and suppress the spread of infectious diseases and other epidemics.  It also authorizes the arrest, apprehension, detention or conditional release of individuals to prevent the introduction, transmission or spread of suspected infectious diseases.  The roles of the concerrned government agencies are also defined in the bill. Furthermore, the bill provides for a notification and reportorial system for the prevention and suppression of the spread of emergency infectious diseases.

rows.abstract: The total electrification of the country has been placed on the shoulders of electric cooperatives (ECs).  The collection of franchise, business, property, value-added and other forms of taxes and imposts on ECs by the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) and some loval government units will deplete the ECs scarce resources rendering it incapable of performing its missionary role.  Taxing ECs of whatever kind is indirectly taxing the poor rural electric cooperative consumers. This bill proposes toextend the tax exemption and privileges granted to ECS from a period of thirty years to a period of fifty years from the date of cooperative organization.

As a general rule, a compromise to the rightto strike is unconstitutiona l and illegl and should not be tolerated. However, due to the need to keep or find employment, laborers and workers are usually compelled to agree to extremely unfavorable conditions. What is occuring in practice and issanctioned by jurisprudence is that the right to strike is not absolute and may be stipulated in CBAs  of employees and labor unions. rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING POLICIES AND MEASURES FOR THE PREVENTION, CONTROL AND TREATMENT OF SEVERE ACUTE RESPIRATORY SYNDROME (SARS), PROVIDING FUNDS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The measure aims to institute policies and measures to immediately control, prevent and treat SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) through the implementation of a comprehensive information program and education campaign. It also proposes to establish a SARS Isolation Center and an Airport Quarantine Area, and the creation of a Philippine national SARS Council.  A comprehensive SARS monitoring program or "Bantay SARS" shall likewise be established under the Department of Health (DOH). It also proposes a system for reporting and contact tracing vis-a-vis other health related intelligence activities by the DOH.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06117

rows.author: C111
rows.title_full: AN ACT CHANGING THE SCHOOL OPENING AND BEGINNING OF CLASSES TO THE FIRST MONDAY OF SEPTEMBER OF EVERY SCHOOL YEAR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to move the school opening and beginning of classes to the first Monday of September of each year for the following reasons :  a) to make the school opening consistent with the rest of the world; b) to avoid the difficulties experienced by school children due to rainy months and floods; and c) to allow the SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) epidemic to pass over during the months of June, July and August, allowing our health authorities to contain, abate and develop remedies for SARS.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING CALAMANSI JUICE AS THE NATIONAL HEALTH DRINK
rows.abstract: The calamansi fruit has long been a staple item in the Filipino dining table. It is used as an ingredient in food dips, a clavoring for dishes and a healthful juice drink. Studies have shown that calamansi is one of the best sources of Vitamin C. This measure seeks to declare calamansi juice as the "National Dealth Drink". Its adoption as a National Health Drink will promote calamanasi to its rightful lofty billing as a very good fruit juice.

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 123 OF 1947, STRENGTHENING THE REGULATORY CAPACITY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH IN QUARANTINE AND INTERNATIONAL HEALTH SURVEILLANCE
rows.abstract: "Bureau of Quarantine Act of 2003".  The recent outbreak of SARS (Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome) has caught many countries flat-footed including the Philippines. This measure proposes to strengthen the Quarantine Law and to change the name of the Bureau of Quarantine Service to the Bureau of Quarantine and International Health Surveillance. It provides for a command and control structure which would not only prevent the outbreak of contagious diseases like SARS from spreading into the country but it also oversees matters such as information dissemination, coordination of responses and other necessary powers in the event that quarantine fails.

rows.title_short: Amending RA 7082, Extending the Franchise Granted to the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company
rows.abstract: RA 7925 (Public Telecommunicati ons Policy Act of the Philippines) liberalized the telecommunicati ons industry and allowed multiple operations by local service providers in partnership with firms of varying nationalities. Section 23 of RA 7925 granted equal treatment to all telecommunicati on companies by allowing them to enjoy the same type of favor, advantage and exemption or immunity. However, the Supreme Court (SC) in the case of PLDT v Davao City, et al, ruled that the grant of tax exemption to one telecommunicati on company should not be construed to mean that said exemption can be enjoyed by another telecommunicati on company. This bill seeks to cure and correct the interpretation made by the SC and seeks to re-enact PLDT's previouus tax exemption to conform to the SC's decision and level the playing field.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2003-08-04, transmitted to on 2003-08-05 and received by the Senate on 2003-08-07

rows.abstract: "National Food Authority Reorganization Act of 2003". The National Food Authority (NFA) is mandated to ensure food security in staple cereals during calamities and emergencies and stability of staple cereal supply and prices. This mandate is considered critical even with the present trend toward trade liberalization and globalization. To enable the NFA to meet its mandate, it must be restructured and its finances strengthened. This bill proposes to strengthen NFA financially and structurally soit will develop into a strong Food Development and Regulatory Administration and a State Financing Enterprise. It also proposes to reorganize the NFA and institute reforms therein.

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE MEAT INSPECTION SYSTEM OF THE PHILIPPINES, INTEGRATING ALL LAWS, RULES AND REGULATIONS PERTINENT TO MEAT AND MEAT PRODUCT EXPORTS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"The Meat Inspection Code of the Philippines\". Meat and meat products are vital components in the food security program of the country.  We must ensure not only an adequate supply of meat and meat products but wwe must also ensure that these are safe and fit for human consumption. Therefore, there is an urgent needto update and strengthen the rules and regulations pertaining to the protection of the health of food animals prior to butchering, the proper and hygienic preparation and preservationof meat and meat products, to strict inspection and marketing of the same. This bill seeks to strengthen and codify the rules and regulations on meat and meat products inspection to ensure their safety and fitness for human consumption.

rows.abstract: Inspite of laws and penalties, film and music piracy has reached an alarming level.  Piracy has caused the decline in revenues of legitimate entertainment business owners which could have helped them power back money into the economy.  This bill seeks the imposition of stricter penalties against violators of PD 1987 to give more teeth to the government's campaign against piracy and thereby protect the legitimate entertainment media industry.  It proposes to impose on violators, upon conviction,a mandatory penalty of six months and one day to three years imprisonment and a fine of not less that PhP500,000 but not more than PhP1.0 million.

rows.title_short: The Personal Equity and Retirement Account (PERA)
rows.abstract: "Personal Equity and Retirement Account". This measure aims to promote the capital market development and savings mobilization by establishing the legal and regulatory framework of retirements plans comprised of voluntary personal savings and investments. Contributors to the personal equity and retirement account (PERA) shall retain ownership of the funds placed therein, including all the earnings of such funds. The PERA Investment Vehicles (common trust fund, mutual fund, annuity contract or pre-need pension plans dedicated solely for PERA purposes) shall be granted tax exemption privileges.
